This is not a game btw, it's a 1:1 simulator of the average evening of any elderly person in Italy after getting their retirement check from INPS.

Here you can experience the generational ritual of "ballarsi la fresca" in first person, and you should be honoured.

The fact that the devs are Italian (I realized that after finding an idol of the Gabibbo as a trinket) just proves that what I wrote above is not just a headcanon, but a documentary.

The first game I played on my Steam Deck and what a great experience. As a big fan of Hollow Knight, this scratched a similar itch, with a much more restrained scope and scale. Bosses were challenging, but fair. They each required careful planning and I enjoyed determining their patterns. My main complaint is that there a few areas that had multiple hyper aggressive enemies on a single screen, which was a pain in the butt to proceed past. Otherwise I absolutely loved the game!

It's basically a game about locals trying to protect their forest from illegal logging and fail.
Every time.

It's a pretty short game but at the same time has so much depth to it! There's a plethora of ways to commit the Deed, which affect the outcome, further the way you use evidence, and the choices you make when talking with people, even the choice of talking or not talking to someone can all have an effect on the final verdict. Really makes it worth and rewarding to replay the game a few times, and if you so desire can just do the worst most clumsy job possible just for the laughs.

Still amazing. Still gorgeous. But much, muuuuuuch more difficult than original game.
Be prepared for broken gamepad. Or fingers. Or both.

P.S. Those who said that Path of Pain in original Hollow Knight was super easy. I hope you're satisfied now

As a pretty big Tomb Raider fan, I was hopeful going into this game. The game does not disappoint whatsoever. The story was 10/10. It was fun, interesting, and always kept me engaged. I went into this game completley blind. I had no idea about the story, or what this game had to offer. The combat is kinda clunky, and made it hard to fight bosses sometimes, but was still fun. I had to lower the combat difficulty to fight Voss, because I was struggling so much (was playing on moderate until that point). Switching the combat difficulty to the easiest was very helpful for that last fight. As a person who sucks at stealth, and combat, it wasn't bad overall. I think the game deserves a 9.5/10 only losing .5 due to the clunky combat.

If you can look past the terrible control mapping and limited keybindings, there is a gem to be found in the rough. The Darkness II has a decently fun gameplay loop, delivering some bloody good gore and a solid enough FPS experience. However, the main takeaway is the lovingly crafted story and characters. Despite The Darkness II's shortcomings, its a solid game at its core. 

If you like DOOM  and/or Wolfenstein, play this.

PRAGMATA is proof that a game can repeatedly humble me and still make me come back for more. Fresh gameplay, wholesome story, and enough emotional damage to make me miss my dad.

Clean fun controls, simplicity that's used as a focus rather than a crutch, and a story I actually care about. If you've ever wondered the realities of trying to do hero stuff while carrying a chunk of steel weighing three times your body weight, GIGASWORD addresses that in its puzzles to great fun effect.

I played through the whole game on steamdeck and absolutely loved it; runs flawlessly and looks great too. The gameplay loop immediately hooked me and I really enjoyed upgrading my ship and exploring the world. The game has such a strong identity with all aspects from the art design and music to the game systems and story working in tandem to create an atmosphere that is both relaxing and creepy. The Lovecraftian/ cosmic horror themes are such a perfect match for this type of game and it can be genuinely scary at times, particularly in the early game, getting caught out at sea when night creeps in makes you feel so panicked as you try to navigate your way through the fog with your only source of light blinking out back to the nearest dock before something finds you. If you haven't played this yet it is definitely worth it and the DLCs are pretty great too. <3

Furi is the result of what would have happened if Journey had been a bullet hell game. It features a fantastic soundtrack, a unique graphical design, good art direction and responsive controls, making this a blast to behold and a game that actually deserves a lot more recognition.

Far Cry 3 came out in 2012 and I just played it now.

It's an interesting and exciting story, but the ending disappointed me. I chose my friends because I saved them throughout the game.The characters are vibrant and well-developed.
The protagonist, Jason Brody, often becomes unhinged, either due to the influence of drugs or the traumatic events he has endured.
The soundtrack is superb, particularly during the mission to burn the plantations.
The companion I met randomly genuinely cared about me and waited for me in the game. We ended up finishing the journey together. What an experience.

I mean for what game is present, it's great. But after RE2 which became (in my eyes) the industry standard remakes should aim for, this is a huge let down. You can beat this game faster than RE4 Separate Ways DLC which tells you all you need to know. Luckily, I think Capcom learnt from this mistake.

But like I said, what is present is great so I would recommend if you are playing through the franchise but just note its not a very big game.

Playing the game requires a Ubisoft Connect account, and you can only link your Steam account to one Ubisoft Connect account. If for whatever reason you lose access to the Ubisoft Connect account your Steam account is linked to, then you have to remove and repurchase the game and create a new Ubisoft Connect account just to be able to play it.

Games that require another account to play a game you purchased should be avoided at all cost.

I put off playing this game for the better part of four years and, looking back , I so much wish that I hadn't. Dishonored is such a brilliant game that now, nine years after its release, it holds up brilliantly. This so perfectly reminds me of a better time in gaming: when games were focused, tight, and truly works of art. These qualities are all too rare in gaming today, and it is because of them that Dishonored rests among my favorite games that I have played in the past couple of years. 

I'm looking forward to doing a high chaos run, picking up the DLCs when they are next on sale, and moving on to Dishonored 2.

Game Dev Tycoon is one of those rare gems that you just keep coming back to. Maybe you don't play it for tens of hours at a time but its enjoyable everytime you give it a go. With the developer also continuing to update the game I think this is a must play for everyone.

I know the Hitman community collectively loses its mind whenever this one gets brought up, but hear me out. Absolution traded the sandbox freedom of Blood Money for a more linear story and yeah, the disguise system got nerfed pretty hard. But 47 sneaking through a diner full of trigger happy nuns? Peak cinema. The story is surprisingly engaging, the gunplay feels satisfying,and the graphics still hold up decently. It's not the best Hitman game, but calling it bad is genuinely a reach. Give it a shot before the purists find you.
[8/10]
